messages:
Maya (devex): FYI I'm hitting certificate verify failures when installing the python SDK inside a Windows venv. repro on 3.8/3.11/3.12.
Maya (devex): pip command used: `python -m venv .venv && .\.venv\Scripts\activate && pip install redwood-inference`
Maya (devex): traceback: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed (_ssl.c:1123)`
Sam (sdk): thanks. are you behind a corporate proxy or custom CA? can you run `python -c "import ssl, certifi; print(ssl.get_default_verify_paths(), certifi.where())"` and paste output?
Liam (windows): on windows many pythons ship with no default cafile path set and pip may use a bundled openssl that doesn't see the Windows cert store. often certifi fixes it.
Maya (devex): output: `DefaultVerifyPaths(cafile=None, capath=None, openssl_cafile_env=None, openssl_cafile=None, openssl_capath_env=None, openssl_capath=None)`
Maya (devex): certifi.where(): `C:\Users\maya\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python311\Lib\site-packages\certifi\cacert.pem`
Jess (qa): CI (linux) installs fine, so this looks windows-specific. QA saw a similar intermittent build failure previously when wheels weren't present.
Sam (sdk): provisional workaround: `pip install certifi && set SSL_CERT_FILE=%(CERTIFI)s` (Windows cmd) where %(CERTIFI)s is the path from certifi.where(). Powershell: `$env:SSL_CERT_FILE=(python -c "import certifi;print(certifi.where())")`.
Maya (devex): workaround allowed install. but onboarding must not require this for users. many will hit this silently.
Sam (sdk): agreed. proposed fixes: 1) produce prebuilt wheels for cp38-cp312-win_amd64 so pip doesn't fall back to sdist build, 2) add support for REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE env var and fallback to certifi if no system cafile found, 3) add Windows note in quickstart.
Liam (windows): when building wheels we should document the MSVC toolchain and OpenSSL version. also ensure the wheel's metadata declares supported_platform correctly.
Jess (qa): add a smoke install job in the Windows matrix for 3.8-3.12 so we catch regressions. we can run a simple `pip install .` and import test.
Maya (devex): another DX issue: AsyncClient typing. mypy/autocomplete returns Any for async methods, which is bad for DX.
Sam (sdk): we've had requests for PEP 561 stubs and typed overloads. let's deliver stubs alongside the wheel release to avoid an extra packaging step.
Sam (sdk): I'll open a meta-issue tracking: wheels + env-bundle + typing stubs + docs + QA job.
pip-bot: created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/421 (windows wheels + ca fallback + typing stubs) :sparkles:
Liam (windows): note for the issue: include which OpenSSL ABI we link so runtime mismatches are minimized.
Jess (qa): assigning the QA matrix to @jess, infra build to @liam, SDK packaging to @sam.
Sam (sdk): adding to next sprint. thanks for the clear repro and workaround, Maya.
Maya (devex): I'll draft the Windows quickstart snippet and PR it to docs repo, plus add the certifi tip under troubleshooting. :memo:
